interpretation.conclusion: The earlier roughly +52.5% reused-closure and +22.3% fresh-closure deltas on PHP 8.4 were not reproduced by the bounded paired ABBA comparison. This does not prove zero overhead or identify scheduling as the cause.
remaining_signals: PHP 8.4 fresh closure: +2.34% aggregate; adjacent pairs +2.08% and +2.61%; process-median ranges overlap.
PHP 8.4 method array: +5.32% aggregate; adjacent pairs +2.03% and +8.74%; both fixed process medians exceed both baseline medians. This is a small residual positive signal.

PHP 8.5 no-argument make: +17.92% aggregate, but fixed medians differ greatly (9391.8 and 7182.5 ns), with adjacent pair deltas +33.25% and +2.50%. A stable regression of the aggregate magnitude is not established.
PHP 8.5 autowire make: +4.53% aggregate with adjacent pair deltas +9.99% and -0.87%, so the earlier roughly +14% effect is not consistently reproduced.
limitations: Only two measured processes per source/runtime; no confidence interval or significance claim.
Each process result is the unmodified RuntimeBench median of seven rounds. Reported ranges are between process medians, not individual-round ranges.
No CPU affinity or scheduler instrumentation was added. Variability is observed; its cause is not proven.
No additional benchmark runs after the requested four valid timed runs per runtime.

paired_runtime_comparison.evidence_note: Raw stderr contained only the parsed precheck/postcheck diagnostics retained above; the repetitive enumeration of 130 source paths per process is omitted. Every loaded DI declaration passed source verification.

interpretation: No end-to-end application throughput or SLA claim.
Large unpaired PHP84 closure increase did not reproduce in the bounded ABBA comparison.
PHP84 method-array showed a positive 5.32 percent aggregate signal; absence of all overhead is not established.
PHP85 make/no-arguments aggregate was +17.92 percent, with pair deltas +33.25 and +2.50 percent; a stable effect of that magnitude is not established.
Two processes per source/runtime do not establish statistical significance. Scheduling was not measured as a cause.
Availability counts are autoload requests observed by one counting callback, not filesystem reads or number of loaded classes.
